bug_description.normalized:
The staged 36-byte witness is not sent verbatim. In `fuzz/driver.cc`, `writer_thread()` treats `
--MARK--
` as a packet delimiter and writes only the prefix before the first marker, so H2O actually receives exactly `\xFF reproxy-test HTTP/1.0

`. `handle_incoming_request()` materializes the raw path token `reproxy-test`; `h2o_req_setup()` normalizes that bare path to `/reproxy-test`, and `setup_pathconf()` selects the reverse-proxy route that the fuzz driver registered for that path. The local upstream helper in `fuzz/driver_common.cc` always returns `HTTP/1.0 200 OK
Connection: Close

Ok` and then closes. In `http1client.c:on_head`, that response is treated as close-delimited: after the response headers are consumed, the trailing `Ok` bytes remain in `client->buf`, and the first `on_body_until_close()` callback reports `size == 2`. `do_send()` then swaps those 2 bytes into `self->sending.buf`, sends them as an in-progress response, and `finalostream_send()` emits headers plus that body chunk while flipping the downstream HTTP/1 ostream state from HEAD to BODY. When `on_send_next()` later drives `do_proceed()`, `h2o_doublebuffer_consume()` drains `self->sending.buf` back to size 0. Only after that does the upstream close reach `on_body_on_close()`: it snapshots the still-empty `client->buf` into `last_content_before_send`, so both `self->sending.buf->size` and `last_content_before_send->size` are 0. The next `h2o_doublebuffer_prepare()` therefore returns `{NULL, 0}`, `do_send()` derives a final `veccnt = 0`, and `h2o_send()` forwards that zero count into `finalostream_send()`. Because the ostream is already in BODY state and chunked encoding was never enabled, `finalostream_send()` keeps `bufcnt == 0` but still calls `h2o_socket_sendvec()`. Vulnerable `h2o_socket_sendvec()` uses that zero count as the VLA bound of `h2o_iovec_t bufs[cnt];`, producing the saved UBSan `non-positive-vla-bound-value`; the patch fixes it by returning `do_write(sock, NULL, 0)` when `cnt == 0`.

sink.description: UBSan crash site. The propagated zero send-vector count is evaluated as the VLA bound of `bufs`, triggering `non-positive-vla-bound-value`.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run reports `/src/h2o/lib/common/socket.c:903:22: runtime error: variable length array bound evaluates to non-positive value 0` with stack `h2o_socket_sendvec -> finalostream_send -> h2o_send`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `h2o_socket_sendvec` assumes `cnt > 0` and declares a VLA from it without a pre-check. The fixing patch inserts `if (cnt == 0) return do_write(sock, NULL, 0);` immediately before this declaration.
root_cause.note: This function already special-cases callback state and flattened-buffer state, but the staged vulnerable source contains no zero-count fast path before the VLA declaration.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled request-path token `reproxy-test` is first materialized here; after normalization it becomes `/reproxy-test` and selects the reverse-proxy handler that reaches the zero-count send path.

parser_admitted.description: After `phr_parse_request()` and `fixup_request()` accept the HTTP/1.0 request and find no request body, the ordinary-request branch stops reading and dispatches the parsed request into handler selection.

evidence_limitations: `trace_feedback.json` required a static repair of the middle chain, but `run_flags.json` keeps `runtime_disambiguation` false, so Stage 02 rebuilt the trace entirely from staged source, patch, saved crash artifacts, and the staged witness without adding instrumentation.

The exact staged checkout that reproduced (`8a76f09d6dfc14418b47962b2a27451ffd226b7d`) differs from the metadata `vulnerable_commit`; this GT is grounded in the staged vulnerable tree because its line map matches the saved UBSan trace and contains the unfixed zero-count VLA.

Stage 01's saved artifacts record the crash and the witness bytes but not per-callback timestamps, so the ordering between the first body-send callback and the later EOF callback is reconstructed from the staged callback structure in `http1client.c`, `proxy.c`, and `http1.c` rather than from a fresh runtime trace.

fine_trace.note:
Source. After the fuzz writer strips everything from the first `
--MARK--
` onward, this parser call reads the socket prefix `\xFF reproxy-test HTTP/1.0

` and materializes raw method/path tokens, including path token `reproxy-test`.
Request setup preserves the raw token `reproxy-test` in `req->path` and normalizes it into `/reproxy-test`, which is the string used for path dispatch.

The normalized path `/reproxy-test` matches the dedicated path that the fuzz driver registered with `h2o_proxy_register_reverse_proxy`, so this request is bound to the reverse-proxy handler rather than the fallback file handler.

The reverse-proxy upstream replies with `HTTP/1.0 200 OK
Connection: Close

Ok`, so the HTTP/1 client leaves `reader` as `on_body_until_close`, marks the response body phase active, consumes only the parsed headers, and immediately re-enters the reader with the trailing body bytes still resident in `sock->input`. Because `setup_client()` bound `client->super.buf` to `sock->input`, those leftover bytes are what proxy code later sees as `self->client->buf`.

The first body callback sees that exactly 2 unread bytes remain after header parsing, adds those bytes to the upstream-body counters, and invokes the proxy's `on_body(NULL)` callback for that non-EOF body chunk.

On the first proxy send, `db` is `self->sending` and `receiving` is `self->client->buf`. Because `self->sending.buf` is empty while `self->client->buf` holds the body `Ok`, this call swaps those 2 bytes into `self->sending.buf`, leaves `self->client->buf` pointing at the old empty buffer, and returns an iovec of length 2.

Because `last_content_before_send` is still NULL and the prepared vector length is 2, this first `do_send()` call takes the non-final branch, derives `veccnt = 1`, marks the send as `H2O_SEND_STATE_IN_PROGRESS`, records 2 body bytes sent, and forwards that single vector downstream.

This first downstream send enters `finalostream_send()` while the HTTP/1 ostream is still in HEAD state, so it emits response headers, flips `conn->_ostr_final.state` to BODY, appends the 2-byte body vector, and calls `h2o_socket_sendvec()` with a non-zero `bufcnt`. Because the request is HTTP/1.0, `setup_chunked()` leaves `chunked_buf == NULL` and no chunk suffix is added.

The non-final send from step 8 uses callback `on_send_next`, which calls `h2o_proceed_response()` and reaches `do_proceed()`. Since `self->sending.inflight` is set, `h2o_doublebuffer_consume()` consumes the entire inflight chunk; here `_bytes_inflight` equals the full 2-byte buffer, so `self->sending.buf->size` becomes 0.

When the upstream helper closes the connection after sending `Ok`, the close-delimited reader re-enters its EOF branch, marks the upstream response closed, and reinvokes the proxy body callback with `h2o_httpclient_error_is_eos`.

EOF detaches the remaining upstream-body buffer into `last_content_before_send`, resets `self->client->buf`, and marks the response complete. On this path the detached buffer is empty: step 6 already swapped the only `Ok` bytes out of `self->client->buf`, and no later body read refilled it before EOF arrived.

The next `do_send()` again calls `h2o_doublebuffer_prepare()` with `db = self->sending` and `receiving = &self->last_content_before_send`. Step 9 drained `self->sending.buf` to size 0 and step 11 detached an empty trailing buffer, so this call returns a zero-length iovec.

With EOF already seen, a zero-length prepared chunk, and an empty detached trailing buffer, `do_send()` takes its final-response branch and derives `veccnt = 0` with `ststate = H2O_SEND_STATE_FINAL` before calling `h2o_send()`.
The proxy generator forwards the final send request with `bufcnt == 0` unchanged into the ostream chain; because the loop does not execute, no body vectors are added before `do_sendvec()` is called.

On the crashing call, the first send has already moved `conn->_ostr_final.state` to BODY and `chunked_buf` is still NULL, so this second `finalostream_send()` invocation adds no headers, appends no body vectors (`inbufcnt == 0`), leaves `bufcnt == 0`, and still calls `h2o_socket_sendvec(..., bufcnt, ...)`.

Root cause and sink. `finalostream_send()` has passed `cnt == 0`, but vulnerable `h2o_socket_sendvec()` has no `cnt == 0` fast path before using that value as a VLA bound. UBSan reports this exact line as `variable length array bound evaluates to non-positive value 0`, and the patch fixes it by returning `do_write(sock, NULL, 0)` before the declaration.

format.name: marker-delimited HTTP/1.0 reverse-proxy witness
format.contract:
The witnessed trigger is exactly the staged 36-byte file whose first packet prefix is `\xFF reproxy-test HTTP/1.0

` and whose remaining bytes begin with the harness delimiter `
--MARK--
`. `writer_thread()` sends only the bytes before that first delimiter, so the server must actually parse raw path token `reproxy-test` (normalized to `/reproxy-test`) and route the request through the reverse-proxy handler. The upstream helper must then return the fixed close-delimited response body `Ok`: the first body callback sends those 2 bytes as an in-progress response and moves `finalostream_send()` from HEAD to BODY, `do_proceed()` consumes that sent chunk, and only the later EOF callback snapshots an empty trailing buffer. That exact sequence is what makes the next final send carry zero vectors into `h2o_socket_sendvec`.
